target: axillary short shoot / leaf fascicle (PO_0004701 short shoot, axillary), negated present, frequency usually
fix: 'axillary leaf cluster' is a compound noun naming a cluster of leaves (a short shoot) in the leaf axil; the head noun 'cluster' is the bearer, not 'leaf'. Compound bearers '<position> <part> cluster/fascicle' must not fall back to the modifier noun.
reason: The flora says the axillary leaf clusters (fascicles) are usually absent; leaves themselves are present (the blade is described just before). 'Leaf absent' is false.

target: leaf + upper (FLOPO_0991376) / perichaetial leaf; fertile belongs to the stem (whole), not to the leaf
fix: Subject phrases 'upper and perichaetial leaves' were reduced to 'leaf'; the 'upper' member-of-series word and the 'on fertile stems' whole must both be carried: the length is of upper/perichaetial leaves of fertile stems.
reason: The 0.5–1.4 mm length belongs to the upper and perichaetial leaves of fertile stems, which are 'much longer than lower leaves'. Without 'upper', it reads as the length of all leaves. Tagging the leaf itself as 'fertile' is also inexact.

target: lanceolate (PATO_0001877) or ovate-lanceolate (no single term; intermediate lanceolate/ovate), with context upper (FLOPO_0991376)
fix: The alternative splitter cut the hyphenated compound 'ovate-lanceolate' and kept only 'ovate'. Hyphenated shape compounds X-Y are one value (Y modified towards X), never X alone.
reason: The flora says lanceolate or ovate-lanceolate, not ovate. The 'upper leaves' position is also not carried (lower leaves are ovate).

fix: Better bearer would be inflorescence branch rather than shoot-axis branch, but the container inflorescence (PO_0009049) makes the meaning right.
reason: The compound cyme is 2- or 3-branched: 2–3 branches within the inflorescence.

target: distal (upper) portion of the leaf, not 'upper leaves' (FLOPO_0991376)
fix: In 'Leaves ..., upper flattened, lower keeled or trigonous on abaxial side' the words upper/lower name the distal and proximal parts of each leaf (typical of Sparganium/monocot leaves), not members of a series. When upper/lower follow a plural part and contrast cross-section shape, read them as part-of-the-part (place), not as which leaves.
reason: Sparganium leaves are flat in their upper part and keeled/trigonous below. The flora does not say the upper leaves are flattened.
Laxly tufted culms means a caespitose (tufted) habit of the whole plant. The modifier 'laxly' is lost but that does not make the statement false.

fix: Bearer could be leaf apex (PO_0020137) via bearer_scope, as in A05439, but acute/acuminate are apex-shape terms conventionally said of the blade.
reason: Leaf blade apex acute to acuminate, a continuum in sharpness. That matches the source.
Involucre 4.5–6 mm in the first (length/height) dimension; the second figure (5–6 mm) is the diameter.
Flowers in racemes, white to pale pink: a colour continuum from white to pale pink. The bud colour is a separate statement.
Petal apex rounded. PATO has no 'rounded' term, so obtuse is the accepted grounding and is substituted onto petal apex.
Stamens 4 (in the staminate flowers just described).

target: lateral stem leaves, falciform with frequency 'sometimes' and qualifier approximately (sub-)
fix: 'sometimes' must go to frequency_qualifier and the prefix 'sub-' to value_qualifier approximately; the subject 'the lateral ones' (lateral leaves, opposed to median leaves) must be kept as position.
reason: Only the lateral leaves are sometimes somewhat falcate; the median leaves are symmetric. 'Leaf falciform' as an unqualified statement is false for this moss.
A didymous capsule is twin-lobed, so fruit bilobed is the right reading.

target: leaf rachis (PO_0020055) — secondary rachis branch of the frond
fix: 'rachis branches' (and 'secondary rachis branches' in Lygodium) are branches of the frond rachis; the word 'branch' after 'rachis' must not map to shoot-axis branch.
reason: In Lygodium the branches are parts of the climbing frond (leaf), not stem branches. The 'not winged' negation itself is right.

fix: 'the base X' / 'base X' after a lamina must be scoped to the base (bearer_scope substituted_bearer, as for 'apex rounded'); cuneate as defined in PATO (narrowly triangular, tapering to the base) is a whole-outline shape and is false of an elliptic lamina.
reason: The lamina is elliptic; only its base is roughly cuneate.
The anthers are 20–24-locellate: 20–24 locelli (compartments) per anther. Locule within the anther is the nearest bearer.

fix: The 'basal leaves' position is not carried; leaf apex would be a more exact bearer.
reason: Basal leaf apex obtuse or acute; the alternatives are correct. Cauline leaf apices are not described otherwise, so it is not false.
Leaves green or greyish green.

target: leaflet base (leaf base PO_0020040 within leaflet), rounded (obtuse PATO_0001935, approximately)
fix: Same cause as A05444: shape words after 'base' were put on the whole part. 'base suborbicular' (FOC wording) means the base is roughly rounded; orbicular as a whole-outline shape must never be given to the part when a 'base' scope word precedes it.
reason: The leaflets are narrowly lanceolate; saying the leaflet is (approximately) orbicular is false.

target: abaxial (lower) lamina surface, place: rims of the areoles
fix: In a clause chain 'upper surface glabrous, lower surface glabrous on the veins, sparsely ... puberulous on the rims of the areoles' the subject 'lower surface' carries over to the following comma-clause; the surface and the place phrase 'on the rims of the areoles' must be kept.
reason: Only the lower surface is puberulous, and only on the areole rims; the upper surface is glabrous. 'Lamina puberulous' with no surface or place overstates it.
Stamens 2.

fix: The exact bearer is the seed-bearing body of the samara (not the wing); no PO term for it, so fruit is acceptable.
reason: The samara body is striate-veined, i.e. striated.
Style longer than stamens.
Leaflets 5–7, rarely up to 9.
The cauline leaves are coriaceous.
Petals slightly shorter than sepals.
The sterile frond lamina is ovate; the sterile context is right.
Stony seeds are hard.
Cymes (inflorescences) shorter than leaves.
10–14 secondary veins on each side of the midvein, in the leaf blade.
